question: Why is busy-time K only 6.8 under local[16] with peak inflight 60?
answer: K_busy = sum(request latency) / union(in-flight intervals) already excludes idle time between queries and between the 5 E2 runs.
Most of that busy union is metadata: 8859 HEAD + 36190 sub-64KiB GETs per run (footer length, footer, page index). Those streams run at K_metadata ≈ 4.2.
Vectored IO is frozen at 4 active ranged reads (s3a_session). K_data ≈ 4.07 matches that cap, not the 16 task slots.
Peak inflight 60 is a brief overlap of task-wave HEADs + footer GETs + a few data GETs (high-inflight is 55% of busy wall, but average concurrent HTTP calls stay ~4–7).

L1 therefore uses K_busy = 6.77 as the single divisor on the sum of HEAD+meta+data request costs. Splitting K_metadata/K_data is documented but not required once the baseline GET/byte gate is within 10%.
